title: Life Processes in Plants
seo_title: Life Processes in Plants Class 7 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10)
standard_code: Class 7, Curiosity Chapter 10: Life Processes in Plants
standard_text: Photosynthesis: raw materials, chlorophyll, sunlight, stomata and the products; testing leaves for starch; modes of nutrition in plants: autotrophic, parasitic, saprotrophic, insectivorous and symbiotic; transport of water and food; transpiration; respiration in plants (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 7 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10: photosynthesis, chlorophyll and stomata, the starch test for leaves, parasites, saprotrophs and insect-eating plants, xylem and phloem, transpiration and respiration in plants. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Green plants make food by photosynthesis.
key_sub: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, with sunlight and chlorophyll.
body_html:
How to think about it

Green plants are autotrophs. In their leaves, chlorophyll traps sunlight, and carbon dioxide (taken in through stomata) and water make glucose, giving out oxygen. The glucose is stored as starch, which turns blue-black with iodine after the leaf is boiled in alcohol to remove chlorophyll.

Some plants get food in other ways: Cuscuta is a parasite, mushrooms are saprotrophs and the pitcher plant traps insects. Xylem carries water up from the roots and phloem carries food from the leaves. Water evaporates from leaves (transpiration), which pulls water up and cools the plant. Plants respire all the time.

Example

Which parts of a variegated leaf make starch?

chlorophyll is needed

Answer: only the green parts

Example

Which tissue carries water?

from roots to leaves

Answer: xylem

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Saying phloem carries water.
  • Forgetting to remove chlorophyll before the iodine test.

faq.q: What are the raw materials and products of photosynthesis?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide and water are used, with sunlight and chlorophyll; glucose (stored as starch) and oxygen are made.
The loss of water vapour from the leaves, mainly through stomata; it pulls water up the plant and cools it.

items.q: Why do desert plants such as cactus have spines instead of leaves?
c: to reduce water loss by transpiration
items.e: The green stem makes food.

items.q: How does transpiration help a plant?
c: it pulls water up from the roots and cools the leaves
items.e: A tall tree pulls water many metres up.

items.q: What do xylem vessels carry?
c: water and minerals from the roots to the leaves
food from the leaves to all parts
items.e: Phloem carries food.

items.q: Which part of a plant is responsible for housing bacteria that fix nitrogen?
items.e: Root nodules of pulses: housing bacteria that fix nitrogen.

items.q: Why do farmers grow pulses in fields?

items.e: This reduces the need for fertilisers.

items.q: Which of these is a product of photosynthesis?

items.q: Which part of a plant is responsible for absorbing water and minerals and holding the plant in the soil?

items.q: What is a heterotroph?

items.e: Animals and fungi are heterotrophs.

items.q: Where in a leaf is chlorophyll found?
c: in chloroplasts inside the leaf cells
items.e: Leaves are green because of it.

items.q: Why is a leaf boiled in alcohol before testing it for starch?

items.e: The leaf becomes pale.

items.q: How does a pitcher plant get extra nutrients?
items.e: It lives in soil poor in nitrogen.

items.q: What is the role of leaves in a plant?

items.q: Which of these is a product of photosynthesis?

items.q: Which part of a plant is responsible for making food by photosynthesis?
items.e: Leaves: making food by photosynthesis.

items.q: Why do plants give out more oxygen than they use during the day?

items.e: At night they only respire.

items.q: In a variegated leaf, which parts turn blue-black with iodine?
items.e: Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: What is photosynthesis?
c: the movement of water up the stem
the process by which green plants make food from carbon dioxide and water using sunlight
the loss of water from leaves
the breaking down of food to release energy
items.e: Chlorophyll captures sunlight.

items.q: A leaf from a plant kept in the dark for two days gives no blue-black colour with iodine. Why?

items.e: Light is needed for photosynthesis.
